crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Routing Across Automated Market Makers
children.blurb: Routing across automated market makers is the practice of choosing and sequencing trades across multiple liquidity pools rather than sending an order to a single pool.

children.name: Yield Strategies in Smart Contracts
children.blurb: Yield strategies in smart contracts cover onchain methods for earning a return on crypto assets by placing them into decentralised finance protocols.

children.name: On-Chain Forensics
children.blurb: On-chain forensics is the practice of tracing activity on public blockchains to identify who moved what, when, and why.

children.name: Stablecoin Stress Testing
children.blurb: Stablecoin stress testing covers the set of analyses that ask how a stablecoin's peg, reserves and redemption process behave under adverse conditions.

children.name: Governance Token Outcomes
children.blurb: Governance token outcomes are the results that follow votes, delegation and proposal execution in token based communities.

sections.body: This section looks at where artificial intelligence meets crypto markets and decentralised finance, the trading venues, lending pools and token systems that run on public blockchains. The work here is practical rather than speculative. Agents and models are used to split large orders across several automated market makers so that price impact stays low, to search smart contract strategies for yield, and to trace funds through public ledgers after a theft. Machine learning also feeds stress tests on stablecoins, checking how reserves and redemption behaviour hold up under runs, and it is used to read governance proposals and voting patterns. The common thread is that blockchains produce a continuous, public record of every trade and transfer, which makes them unusually good ground truth for testing AI methods on real money and real incentives.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Some parts of this field are settled. Order routing across automated market makers is well studied, and the basic mechanics of splitting a trade to reduce slippage are understood, though execution still degrades when liquidity thins or gas costs spike. On-chain forensics has become a genuine industry, with clustering and flow analysis used by exchanges and investigators, but it remains probabilistic and determined adversaries can obscure trails. Yield strategies are the least settled area, because returns shift with pool incentives and are often eaten by fees, impermanent loss or contract risk. Stablecoin stress testing is limited by short history and by reserves that are only partly observable, and governance token work struggles with small samples and with votes that are cheap to cast but costly to interpret. Nothing here predicts prices, and no model removes the risk of loss.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The five pages form a chain from execution to governance. Routing Across Automated Market Makers is the entry point, covering how trades are placed and split, and it sets up the cost questions that the rest of the section assumes. Yield Strategies in Smart Contracts follows the money once it is parked, examining how returns are generated and what can go wrong in the code. On-Chain Forensics then turns to the ledger as evidence, tracing flows after failures and attacks, which is also the natural companion to Stablecoin Stress Testing, where the question is whether a peg holds when many holders exit at once. Governance Token Outcomes closes the loop by asking what voting rights and token incentives actually produce over time. A reader new to the area should start with routing, while someone interested in risk should go to stress testing and forensics first.
